sidebar_label: List, filter and search
description: Read the items you need a page at a time, narrowed by type, tags and properties, found by the words they hold, or looked up by title.
job: A builder finds the items an app needs among those a credential can read.
kind: how-to

A listing holds only what its credential can read. In the TypeScript examples, `marfa` is a client made as [the TypeScript SDK](/reference/typescript-sdk#create-a-client) shows.

## List a page at a time

[List items](/reference/api/items/listItems) answers 50 items, or up to 500 if you ask. This lists the files tagged `home`, 20 at a time:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa items list --type core.file --tag home --limit 20 --all
```

```http tab="HTTP"
GET /items?type=core.file&tags=home&limit=20
Authorization: Bearer <key>
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
import { pages } from "@withmarfa/client";

const files = pages(async (cursor) => {
  const { data, error } = await marfa.GET("/items", {
    params: { query: { type: "core.file", tags: "home", limit: 20, cursor } },
  });
  if (error) throw new Error(error.error.message);
  return data;
});
for await (const file of files) console.log(file);
```

The answer holds the page in `data` and a cursor in `next_cursor`. Send `next_cursor` back as `cursor`, with the same query, for the next page.

**Stop only when `next_cursor` is `null`**: a page can be short, even empty, with more after it. `--all` and `pages` follow the cursor for you. A search and a view's items page the same way.

## Narrow a listing

With no parameters, a listing holds the **active items** of every type you can read, in both tiers, newest first by `created_at`. These narrow it, in any combination:

| Parameter | Keeps |
| --- | --- |
| `type` | Up to 10 types, each with every type beneath it. A pattern such as `core.*` matches every type under the prefix. |
| `tags` | Items that carry every tag named. |
| `state` | One or more states, such as `active` and `archived`, or `any` on its own. |
| `tier` | `library` or `feed` items. |
| `source` | Items one writer created. |
| `occurred_after`, `occurred_before` | Items whose `occurred_at`, or `created_at` without one, falls strictly between two times. |
| `backref[<edge type>]` | The items a given item points to by that edge: `backref[parent-of]=<id>` lists an item's children. |
| `beneath` | An item and everything under it by `parent-of`. |

Over HTTP a parameter with several values takes a comma-separated list. In the CLI, repeat the option. `include=metadata` adds each item's tags and extensions, and `include=edges` its edges. **`sort`** orders by `created_at`, `updated_at`, `occurred_at`, `last_activity_at` or `properties.<name>`, with `direction` as `asc` or `desc`, and items that lack a sorted property come last either way.

## Filter by properties

A `filter` is one or more conditions of the form `<field> <operator> <value>`, **joined by `AND` or by `OR`, not both**. A property is `properties.<name>`. This finds the images tagged `home`:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa items list --type core.file \
  --filter 'properties.mime_type starts_with "image/" AND tags contains "home"'
```

```http tab="HTTP"
GET /items?type=core.file&filter=properties.mime_type%20starts_with%20%22image%2F%22%20AND%20tags%20contains%20%22home%22
Authorization: Bearer <key>
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const { data } = await marfa.GET("/items", {
  params: {
    query: {
      type: "core.file",
      filter: 'properties.mime_type starts_with "image/" AND tags contains "home"',
    },
  },
});
```

The operators are `eq`, `neq`, `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`, `contains`, `starts_with`, `exists` and `not_exists`. Strings take double quotes. For a property that is missing or `null`, use `not_exists`: Marfa refuses a comparison with `null`. Four fields reach further:

- **`status_group`** tests the group of an item's [status word](/catalog/field-kinds): `not_started`, `in_progress`, `completed` or `canceled`.
- **`edge[<edge type>]`** finds the items with that edge to a given item, such as a collection's members.
- **`properties.<field>.<member>`** matches any entry of a list, with `eq` only.
- **`part`** tests whether an item is a [part](/build/edges) of another, such as an attached file.

A filter holds at most 10 conditions in 2,048 characters, and works the same in a [saved view](/build/views) and a [working copy](/build/write-in-a-working-copy). The [search and filters](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/search-and-filters.md) chapter of the contract has the grammar. Marfa refuses a query it can't answer exactly, so a typo can't return everything: [Errors](/reference/errors) lists each refusal.

## Search

[Search items](/reference/api/search/searchItems) finds items by the words they hold, best match first:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa search "boiler" --type core.file --type core.task
```

```http tab="HTTP"
GET /search?q=boiler&type=core.file,core.task
Authorization: Bearer <key>
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const { data } = await marfa.GET("/search", {
  params: { query: { q: "boiler", type: "core.file,core.task" } },
});
```

Each entry holds the `item`, its `metadata`, a `relevance_score` and a `snippet_html`, such as `Service the <mark>boiler</mark>`, which escapes the item's text and **is safe to show as HTML**.

**Every word** in `q` must match, in any order, in the item's [searched fields](/catalog/items#searched-fields) or its tags. Words match by stem, the last word matches as a prefix, and double quotes match a phrase. A search answers 20 entries, or up to 100, never matches an item in the bin, and takes a listing's narrowing parameters and `filter`, except `beneath` and `backref[]`.

## Look up items by title

[Find items by title](/reference/api/items/findItemsByTitle) turns up to 200 names a person typed, such as the target of `[[Reading list]]`, into items, and answers one entry for each name, in order:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa items titles "Reading list" Plans
```

```http tab="HTTP"
POST /items/titles
Authorization: Bearer <key>
Content-Type: application/json

{ "names": ["Reading list", "Plans"] }
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const { data } = await marfa.POST("/items/titles", {
  body: { names: ["Reading list", "Plans"] },
});
```

A name that titles nothing gets no `items`, and one that titles several gets them all, so the person can choose. **The whole title must match**, ignoring case and blank characters at either end. Only items the credential can list count, in the bin or not. A name that matches more than 20 items answers the first 20 with `more` set to `true`, so treat it as naming no one item.

## Count items

[Get item counts](/reference/api/items/getItemStats) counts what a listing would match, by state, or by type or source with `by`. It **counts every state unless you name one**, the bin included, in the CLI too: only HTTP takes `state` to name one.

<Terminal>

```bash
marfa items stats --by type
```

```text
core.bookmark      1
core.media.book    3
core.note          7
```

</Terminal>

[Count item links](/reference/api/items/countItemLinks) counts what sits under each of up to 100 items by an edge type, such as the members of each collection.
